experiments.name: 16:8 Intermittent Fasting
experiments.hypothesis: 16:8 fasting for 30 days will reduce fasting glucose by ≥5 mg/dL and support weight loss trend.
experiments.result_summary: The simplest dietary intervention — you don't change what you eat, just when. The 16-hour fast does the rest.
experiments.evidence_citation: Wilkinson et al., Cell Metabolism 2020

experiments.name: 40g Protein at Breakfast
experiments.hypothesis: 40g protein at breakfast for 30 days will reduce total daily caloric intake and support weight loss trajectory.
experiments.result_summary: Front-loading protein changes the entire day. You eat less later without trying.
experiments.evidence_citation: Leidy et al., American Journal of Clinical Nutrition 2015

experiments.name: Active Recovery Day Protocol
experiments.hypothesis: Replacing passive rest days with active recovery for 30 days will maintain recovery scores above baseline.
experiments.result_summary: Rest doesn't mean stillness. The body recovers faster when it moves — just not hard.
experiments.evidence_citation: No direct study verified
experiments.citation_note: The sauna–mortality cohort previously cited here (Laukkanen et al., JAMA Internal Medicine 2015) measures cardiovascular mortality, not recovery markers, and does not support the active-recovery claim. No direct controlled trial of an active-recovery day protocol was verified for this entry.

experiments.name: Ashwagandha — Cortisol/Stress
experiments.hypothesis: 600mg KSM-66 ashwagandha for 60 days will improve HRV by ≥8% and sleep score by ≥3 pts.
experiments.result_summary: The most-studied adaptogen. If cortisol is the slow killer, ashwagandha is the evidence-based counter.
experiments.evidence_citation: Chandrasekhar et al., Indian J Psychological Medicine 2012

experiments.name: Berberine — Glucose Attenuation
experiments.hypothesis: 500mg Berberine before high-carb meals will reduce CGM peaks above 140 mg/dL by ≥20%.
experiments.result_summary: Nature's metformin. The glucose data on this compound is hard to argue with.
experiments.evidence_citation: Yin et al., Metabolism 2008

experiments.name: Box Breathing 5 Minutes Daily
experiments.hypothesis: 5 minutes of box breathing daily for 14 days will increase morning HRV by ≥5%.
experiments.result_summary: Five minutes. No equipment. Direct parasympathetic lever. The simplest measurable intervention for stress.
experiments.evidence_citation: Zaccaro et al., Frontiers in Human Neuroscience 2018

experiments.name: Breathwork Before Sleep
experiments.hypothesis: 5 minutes of 4-7-8 breathing before bed for 14 days will increase pre-sleep HRV and reduce sleep onset latency.
experiments.result_summary: Free. Takes 5 minutes. The extended exhale is a direct parasympathetic lever.
experiments.evidence_citation: Ma et al., Frontiers in Psychology 2017

experiments.name: Bulletproof Sleep Schedule
experiments.hypothesis: Perfect sleep consistency (±15 min) for 30 days will improve average recovery score by >10%.
experiments.result_summary: The newest sleep research says consistency may matter more than duration. This is the hardest sleep experiment and potentially the most impactful.
experiments.evidence_citation: Windred et al., Sleep 2024

experiments.name: Call a Friend/Family Member Weekly
experiments.hypothesis: One phone call per week to a friend/family member for 30 days will deepen at least 2 relationships.
experiments.result_summary: Men are terrible at maintaining friendships. A weekly call is the minimum viable dose for not disappearing from people's lives.
experiments.evidence_citation: Holt-Lunstad et al., PLOS Medicine 2010; Kumar & Epley, J Experimental Psychology 2021

experiments.name: Cold Bedroom Protocol
experiments.hypothesis: Sleeping at 65°F for 14 days will increase deep sleep percentage by ≥10% vs baseline.
experiments.result_summary: Most people sleep in rooms that are too warm. A $0 thermostat adjustment can outperform most sleep supplements.
experiments.evidence_citation: Harding et al., Frontiers in Neuroscience 2019

experiments.name: Cold Exposure + Breathwork Combo
experiments.hypothesis: Daily cold+breathwork for 30 days will improve HRV and recovery scores beyond baseline.
experiments.result_summary: The hardest 5 minutes of the day. Cold wakes the body up. Breathwork calms it back down. The combination teaches regulation under stress.
experiments.evidence_citation: Kox et al., PNAS 2014

experiments.name: Cold Plunge 2 min, 3x/Week
experiments.hypothesis: Cold plunge (2 min, 3x/week) will increase morning HRV and improve subjective mood scores
experiments.result_summary: Deliberate cold exposure for dopamine and mood
experiments.evidence_citation: Šrámek et al., European Journal of Applied Physiology 2000

experiments.name: Cold Shower Every Morning
experiments.hypothesis: Cold showers (2 min) every morning for 30 days will increase morning HRV by ≥5% vs baseline.
experiments.result_summary: The hardest thing you do all day, done first. Two minutes of discomfort that rewires your relationship with avoidance.
experiments.evidence_citation: Buijze et al., PLOS ONE 2016

experiments.name: Community Event Once Per Month
experiments.hypothesis: Attending one community event per month for 90 days will expand the outer social ring by ≥3 acquaintances.
experiments.result_summary: Male loneliness is an epidemic. The cure isn't more texting — it's showing up in a room with other people.
experiments.evidence_citation: No direct study verified — trade book: Dunbar, How Many Friends Does One Person Need? 2010
experiments.citation_note: Dunbar's social-layer work is summarised in a trade book here rather than cited to a specific paper. No peer-reviewed trial of monthly community-event attendance was verified.

experiments.name: Consistent Bedtime Routine
experiments.hypothesis: Following the same 3-step bedtime routine for 30 days will establish a reliable sleep cue.
experiments.result_summary: Rituals aren't woo — they're conditioning. Your brain learns that step 1 means sleep is coming.
experiments.evidence_citation: Mindell et al., Sleep 2009 (pediatric, mechanism applies to adults)

experiments.name: Creatine Monohydrate — Strength
experiments.hypothesis: 5g daily creatine for 56 days will produce ≥8% increase in major lift 1RMs vs pre-supplementation baseline.
experiments.result_summary: The most evidence-backed supplement in existence. If you're lifting and not taking creatine, you're leaving gains on the table.
experiments.evidence_citation: Kreider et al., J Int Soc Sports Nutrition 2017

experiments.name: Creatine: Morning vs Evening
experiments.hypothesis: Switching creatine from evening to morning dosing will maintain cognitive benefits without disrupting sleep metrics.
experiments.result_summary: Creatine is one of the most studied supplements. Timing optimization is the next frontier after confirming the dose.
experiments.evidence_citation: Avgerinos et al., Experimental Gerontology 2018

experiments.name: Daily 8,000+ Steps
experiments.hypothesis: Hitting 8,000+ steps every day for 30 days will improve recovery scores and support weight trend.
experiments.result_summary: Steps are the background radiation of fitness. They don't feel like exercise — that's the point.
experiments.evidence_citation: Saint-Maurice et al., JAMA 2020

experiments.name: Daily Cold Exposure
experiments.hypothesis: Daily cold exposure for 21 days will increase baseline HRV and improve subjective mood scores.
experiments.result_summary: Cold stress is a hormetic stressor — controlled discomfort that builds resilience. The mood and focus benefits are near-immediate.
experiments.evidence_citation: Søberg et al., Cell Reports Medicine 2021

experiments.name: Dairy Elimination
experiments.hypothesis: Removing dairy for 21 days then reintroducing will reveal whether dairy contributes to inflammation, digestive issues, or skin problems.
experiments.result_summary: You can't know if dairy affects you without removing it completely. The reintroduction phase is where the signal appears.
experiments.evidence_citation: Turnbull et al., Alimentary Pharmacology & Therapeutics 2015

experiments.name: Date Night Per Week
experiments.hypothesis: Weekly date nights for 60 days will improve relationship satisfaction and become a protected ritual.
experiments.result_summary: Proximity is not connection. A scheduled date night sounds unromantic — until it becomes the best night of the week.
experiments.evidence_citation: Dew & Wilcox, J Marriage & Family 2011

experiments.name: Deep Work Block (2 Hours)
experiments.hypothesis: A daily 2-hour deep work block for 30 days will increase high-quality output and reduce perceived busyness.
experiments.result_summary: Two hours of real focus produces more than eight hours of multitasking. The problem isn't time — it's attention.
experiments.evidence_citation: Mark et al., CHI 2008; Newport, Deep Work 2016

experiments.name: Digital-Free Dinner
experiments.hypothesis: Phone-free dinners for 14 days will improve mealtime conversation quality.
experiments.result_summary: The phone on the table is a third person in every conversation. Remove it and watch what happens.
experiments.evidence_citation: Przybylski & Weinstein, J Social & Personal Relationships 2013

experiments.name: Dopamine Reset Weekend
experiments.hypothesis: One low-stimulation weekend per month for 30 days will improve weekday focus and reduce compulsive phone checking.
experiments.result_summary: Modern life is a firehose of dopamine. Periodic withdrawal teaches your brain to find satisfaction in ordinary experience.
experiments.evidence_citation: No direct study verified — trade book: Lembke, Dopamine Nation 2021
experiments.citation_note: The source is a trade book. The receptor-sensitivity mechanism is extrapolated from addiction neuroscience; no trial of a weekend 'dopamine reset' was verified.

experiments.name: Evening Shutdown Routine
experiments.hypothesis: A consistent 5-step shutdown routine for 30 days will create clear work/rest boundaries.
experiments.result_summary: Work bleeds into rest because there's no boundary. A ritual draws the line your brain won't draw by itself.
experiments.evidence_citation: Smit & Barber, J Occupational Health Psychology 2016; Newport, Deep Work 2016

experiments.name: Fiber Target ≥30g/Day
experiments.hypothesis: Hitting ≥30g fiber daily for 30 days will reduce glucose variability and support weight trend.
experiments.result_summary: Most Americans get 15g of fiber. Doubling it changes your gut, your glucose, and your satiety.
experiments.evidence_citation: Reynolds et al., The Lancet 2019

experiments.name: Fiber-First Meal Order
experiments.hypothesis: Eating fiber/vegetables before carbohydrates for 14 days will reduce average glucose spikes by >20%.
experiments.result_summary: Same food, different glucose response. This is the simplest dietary hack with the strongest CGM evidence.
experiments.evidence_citation: Shukla et al., Diabetes Care 2015

experiments.name: Fixed Wake Time
experiments.hypothesis: Waking within ±15 min of {target_time} for 30 days will improve average HRV by ≥5% and sleep score by ≥3 points vs baseline.
experiments.result_summary: Your body doesn't know it's Saturday. The most powerful sleep hack isn't a supplement — it's consistency.
experiments.evidence_citation: Wittmann et al., Chronobiology International 2006

experiments.name: Gratitude Log (3 Items/Day)
experiments.hypothesis: Logging 3 specific gratitudes daily for 30 days will measurably improve mood and wellbeing scores.
experiments.result_summary: The brain defaults to scanning for threats. Gratitude practice rewires it to scan for good. Specificity is the key — generic gratitude doesn't stick.
experiments.evidence_citation: Emmons & McCullough, JPSP 2003

experiments.name: Grip Strength Training 3x/Week
experiments.hypothesis: Dedicated grip training 3x/week for 60 days will increase grip strength by ≥10% vs baseline.
experiments.result_summary: Grip strength predicts how long you'll live better than blood pressure does. It's also the first thing to go.
experiments.evidence_citation: Leong et al., The Lancet 2015

experiments.name: Hydration Target
experiments.hypothesis: Hitting hydration target daily for 14 days will become habitual.
experiments.result_summary: Most people are mildly dehydrated most of the time. It's the most boring intervention that actually matters.
experiments.evidence_citation: Popkin et al., Nutrition Reviews 2010

experiments.name: Journaling Before Bed
experiments.hypothesis: Journaling for 10 minutes before bed for 30 days will become habitual and reduce time-to-sleep.
experiments.result_summary: Writing is thinking made visible. The brain that dumps its contents onto a page sleeps better than the one carrying it all to bed.
experiments.evidence_citation: Scullin et al., J Experimental Psychology 2018; Pennebaker & Beall, J Abnormal Psychology 1986

experiments.name: L-Theanine for Focus
experiments.hypothesis: 200mg L-theanine with morning coffee for 14 days will improve subjective focus and reduce caffeine jitteriness.
experiments.result_summary: The caffeine smoothing agent. Same energy, less edge. The combo is better than either alone.
experiments.evidence_citation: Owen et al., Nutritional Neuroscience 2008

experiments.name: Largest Meal at Lunch
experiments.hypothesis: Eating the largest meal at lunch for 30 days will improve fasting glucose and sleep quality.
experiments.result_summary: Your body processes food better when the sun is up. Dinner is tradition, not biology.
experiments.evidence_citation: Garaulet et al., International J of Obesity 2013

experiments.name: Learning Something New 15 Min/Day
experiments.hypothesis: 15 minutes of daily novel learning for 30 days will build a consistent learning habit.
experiments.result_summary: The brain that stops learning starts declining. Fifteen minutes is the minimum effective dose for novelty.
experiments.evidence_citation: Park et al., Psychological Science 2014

experiments.name: Magnesium Glycinate Before Bed
experiments.hypothesis: 400mg magnesium glycinate before bed for 30 days will increase deep sleep % by ≥8% vs baseline.
experiments.result_summary: Most adults are magnesium-deficient. This is one of the best-studied, lowest-risk sleep supplements.
experiments.evidence_citation: Abbasi et al., J Res Med Sci 2012

experiments.name: Make Bed Immediately on Waking
experiments.hypothesis: Making the bed immediately on waking for 30 days will establish a keystone habit.
experiments.result_summary: The smallest possible win. If you can't do this, nothing else in the system matters. If you can, everything else gets easier.
experiments.evidence_citation: No direct study verified — trade books: Duhigg, The Power of Habit 2012; McRaven, Make Your Bed 2017
experiments.citation_note: Both sources are trade books. As the entry's own summary states, there is no direct biomarker evidence for bed-making as a keystone habit.

experiments.name: Meditation 10 Minutes Daily
experiments.hypothesis: 10 minutes of daily meditation for 30 days will improve HRV by ≥5% and reduce subjective stress.
experiments.result_summary: The most studied mental health intervention that isn't therapy or medication. Ten minutes. Sit still. That's it.
experiments.evidence_citation: Goyal et al., JAMA Internal Medicine 2014

experiments.name: Morning Mobility Routine
experiments.hypothesis: A consistent 10-minute morning mobility routine for 30 days will become automatic and improve subjective readiness.
experiments.result_summary: The body you wake up in isn't the body you had yesterday. Ten minutes of movement reminds your joints they exist.
experiments.evidence_citation: Behm & Chaouachi, European J Applied Physiology 2011

experiments.name: Morning Pages
experiments.hypothesis: 30 days of morning pages will reduce decision fatigue scores and improve subjective mental clarity.
experiments.result_summary: Externalizes the mental chatter that otherwise runs in background loops. Anecdotally transformative for many practitioners.
experiments.evidence_citation: No direct study verified — trade book: Cameron, The Artist's Way 1992
experiments.citation_note: Morning Pages is a practice from a trade book. The adjacent expressive-writing literature (see the Expressive Writing entry) studies a different, prompted protocol.

experiments.name: Morning Sunlight + Evening Blue Blockers
experiments.hypothesis: Combined morning sunlight + evening blue blockers will reduce sleep onset latency and increase deep sleep %
experiments.result_summary: Full circadian protocol: morning light + evening protection
experiments.evidence_citation: Chang et al., PNAS 2015

experiments.name: Morning Sunlight Exposure
experiments.hypothesis: 10 minutes of morning sunlight within 30 min of waking for 30 days will improve sleep onset consistency.
experiments.result_summary: Your eyes set your clock. The Pacific Northwest makes this harder — which makes it more important.
experiments.evidence_citation: Blume et al., Somnologie 2019

experiments.name: NMN — NAD+ Precursor Stack
experiments.hypothesis: 250mg NMN daily for 112 days will produce measurable improvement in HRV (≥8%) and subjective energy.
experiments.result_summary: NAD+ declines with age. If you can raise it back, the downstream effects touch everything from DNA repair to mitochondrial function.
experiments.evidence_citation: Yoshino et al., Science 2021

experiments.name: No Alcohol for 30 Days
experiments.hypothesis: 30 days without alcohol will improve HRV by ≥10%, sleep score by ≥5 pts, and support weight loss.
experiments.result_summary: Alcohol is the most socially accepted compound that wrecks every biomarker we track. Thirty days reveals the real cost.
experiments.evidence_citation: Colrain et al., Handbook of Clinical Neurology 2014

experiments.name: No Caffeine After 12pm
experiments.hypothesis: Eliminating caffeine after 12pm for 30 days will reduce sleep latency and increase deep sleep % by ≥10%.
experiments.result_summary: That 2pm coffee costs you 30 minutes of deep sleep tonight. Most people don't feel it — the data shows it.
experiments.evidence_citation: Drake et al., J Clin Sleep Med 2013

experiments.name: No News/Social Media Before 10am
experiments.hypothesis: No news or social media before 10am for 14 days will improve morning focus and reduce reactive thinking.
experiments.result_summary: The first thing you consume sets the frame for the day. Other people's emergencies are not yours.
experiments.evidence_citation: No direct study verified — trade book: Newport, Digital Minimalism 2019
experiments.citation_note: The rationale rests on a trade book and practitioner consensus. No peer-reviewed trial of delaying morning news/social-media intake was verified.

experiments.name: No Screens Before Bed
experiments.hypothesis: Eliminating screens 60 minutes before bed for 30 days will reduce subjective sleep onset latency and improve sleep consistency.
experiments.result_summary: The screen is the last thing most people see before sleep and the first thing they see after. Breaking that loop is the simplest sleep intervention that exists.
experiments.evidence_citation: Chang et al., PNAS 2015

experiments.name: Omega-3 High Dose (3g EPA+DHA)
experiments.hypothesis: 3g EPA+DHA daily for 60 days will improve HRV and reduce RHR.
experiments.result_summary: The dose most people take (1g) is below therapeutic threshold. Three grams is where the evidence lives.
experiments.evidence_citation: Bhatt et al., NEJM 2019 (REDUCE-IT)

experiments.name: One Deep Conversation per Week
experiments.hypothesis: One intentionally deep conversation per week for 30 days will improve social pillar score and mood.
experiments.result_summary: The loneliness epidemic isn't about being alone — it's about being surrounded by people and feeling unknown.
experiments.evidence_citation: No direct study verified — trade book: Murthy, Together 2020
experiments.citation_note: The source is a trade book synthesising loneliness research rather than a specific trial. No peer-reviewed study of a weekly deep-conversation protocol was verified.

experiments.name: One Meaningful Conversation Per Day
experiments.hypothesis: One meaningful conversation daily for 30 days will shift social interaction quality measurably upward.
experiments.result_summary: Most days are filled with transactional words. One real exchange changes the texture of the entire day.
experiments.evidence_citation: Mehl et al., Psychological Science 2010

experiments.name: Pennebaker Expressive Writing
experiments.hypothesis: Structured expressive writing for 28 days will improve mood scores and reduce anxiety indicators.
experiments.result_summary: The most replicated finding in therapeutic writing research. Works by externalizing and organizing emotional experience.
experiments.evidence_citation: Pennebaker & Beall, Journal of Abnormal Psychology 1986

experiments.name: Post-Dinner Walk
experiments.hypothesis: Walking 10 minutes after dinner for 30 days will reduce post-meal glucose spikes by ≥20% vs baseline.
experiments.result_summary: The post-dinner walk is the most underrated intervention in metabolic health. Ten minutes. No gear. No app. Just gravity and glucose.
experiments.evidence_citation: Buffey et al., Sports Medicine 2022

experiments.name: Pre-Meal Apple Cider Vinegar
experiments.hypothesis: ACV before high-carb meals for 14 days will reduce post-meal glucose peaks by ≥15%.
experiments.result_summary: A tablespoon of vinegar for a 20% reduction in glucose spikes. The cost-benefit ratio is absurd.
experiments.evidence_citation: Shishehbor et al., Diabetes Research and Clinical Practice 2017

experiments.name: Reading 10 Pages a Day
experiments.hypothesis: Reading 10 pages daily for 30 days will establish a consistent reading habit.
experiments.result_summary: Ten pages is nothing. That's the point. The barrier is so low that skipping feels ridiculous. Fifteen books a year changes how you think.
experiments.evidence_citation: Bavishi et al., Social Science & Medicine 2016

experiments.name: Sauna Protocol 2x/Week
experiments.hypothesis: Sauna 2x/week for 30 days will improve HRV and recovery scores compared to baseline.
experiments.result_summary: Finnish longitudinal data shows dose-dependent mortality reduction with sauna frequency. This tests the minimum effective dose.
experiments.evidence_citation: Laukkanen et al., JAMA Internal Medicine 2015

experiments.name: Single-Tasking Blocks
experiments.hypothesis: Single-tasking blocks for 14 days will reduce context-switching and improve work satisfaction.
experiments.result_summary: Tab switching is the fidgeting of the knowledge worker. Training yourself out of it is a competitive advantage.
experiments.evidence_citation: Ophir et al., PNAS 2009

experiments.name: Stretching Before Bed
experiments.hypothesis: 10 minutes of stretching before bed for 14 days will improve sleep quality score.
experiments.result_summary: Your body carries the tension of the day into bed. Ten minutes of unwinding is a physical signal that work is over.
experiments.evidence_citation: Banno et al., PeerJ 2018

experiments.name: Talk to a Stranger Daily
experiments.hypothesis: Daily stranger conversations for 14 days will increase social confidence and improve daily mood ratings.
experiments.result_summary: Social muscles atrophy. This is the gym for your social confidence. Most people find it's far less scary than expected.
experiments.evidence_citation: Epley & Schroeder, Journal of Experimental Psychology 2014

experiments.name: Time-Restricted Eating (12pm-8pm)
experiments.hypothesis: 8-hour eating window (12pm-8pm) will reduce fasting glucose variability and improve time-in-range
experiments.result_summary: 8-hour eating window for metabolic benefits
experiments.evidence_citation: Sutton et al., Cell Metabolism 2018

experiments.name: Tongkat Ali — Recovery Optimization
experiments.hypothesis: 400mg daily Tongkat Ali for 84 days will improve WHOOP recovery score by ≥5 points.
experiments.result_summary: One of the few non-prescription compounds with human trial data on testosterone and cortisol modulation.
experiments.evidence_citation: Talbott et al., J Int Soc Sports Nutrition 2013

experiments.name: Track Everything for 7 Days
experiments.hypothesis: 7 days of perfect tracking compliance will establish a personal best and reveal friction points.
experiments.result_summary: Seven days of perfect data is the diagnostic tool. It shows you where the system works and where it breaks.
experiments.evidence_citation: Burke et al., J American Dietetic Association 2011

experiments.name: Vegetable Volume Loading
experiments.hypothesis: Adding 2 cups of vegetables to every meal for 30 days will reduce total caloric intake and support weight loss.
experiments.result_summary: You can't outeat two cups of broccoli. Volume is the satiety lever most people never pull.
experiments.evidence_citation: Rolls et al., Journal of the American Dietetic Association 2004

experiments.name: Vice Elimination Sprint
experiments.hypothesis: Eliminating one vice completely for 30 days will extend the vice streak and reveal dependency patterns.
experiments.result_summary: You don't know what something costs you until you stop paying. Pick the vice you're most afraid to quit — that's the one.
experiments.evidence_citation: No direct study verified — trade book: Baumeister & Tierney, Willpower 2011
experiments.citation_note: The source is a trade book. No peer-reviewed trial of a fixed-length single-vice abstinence sprint was verified.

experiments.name: Vitamin D Optimization (5000 IU)
experiments.hypothesis: 5000 IU Vitamin D3 daily for 90 days will raise 25(OH)D level to ≥50 ng/mL.
experiments.result_summary: Living in Seattle and not supplementing Vitamin D is a guaranteed deficiency. This is the most obvious supplement for the Pacific Northwest.
experiments.evidence_citation: Holick, NEJM 2007

experiments.name: Weekly Appreciation Message
experiments.hypothesis: Sending one appreciation message per week for 30 days will strengthen at least 3 relationships.
experiments.result_summary: Most people never hear that they matter to you. The message you think about sending but don't — send that one.
experiments.evidence_citation: Kumar & Epley, Psychological Science 2018

experiments.name: Zone 2 Cardio 150+ min/Week
experiments.hypothesis: 150+ min/week Zone 2 for 8 weeks will improve cardiac efficiency (pace-at-HR) by >5%
experiments.result_summary: Sustained Zone 2 base building for 8 weeks
experiments.evidence_citation: Bull et al., British Journal of Sports Medicine 2020 (WHO physical-activity guidelines)

experiments.name: Zone 2 Cardio 3x/Week
experiments.hypothesis: 3+ Zone 2 sessions per week for 60 days will reduce RHR by ≥3 bpm and improve HRV by ≥8%.
experiments.result_summary: Cardiorespiratory fitness is the single strongest predictor of longevity. Zone 2 is where you build it.
experiments.evidence_citation: Mandsager et al., JAMA Network Open 2018
